class.name: HWVideoTexture
class.brief_description: Shows the frames of a [V4L2Decoder] with no copy.
class.description: Plays a raw Annex-B file ([method open]) or the video of a [MediaSource] ([method open_source]). Imports every decoder CAPTURE buffer once as a [DmabufImage], shows the frame that is due at the clock through two plane textures ([method get_plane_texture]), and gives buffers back to the decoder once the GPU is done with them. Call [method update] once per frame from the main thread. Sample plane 0 (Y) with [code].r[/code] and plane 1 (CbCr) with [code].ra[/code], and crop to [method get_visible_uv_rect]: the decoder pads the height.

method.name: close
method.description: Frees the imported buffers and closes the decoder.

method.name: get_decoded_size
method.description: Returns the size of the decoder buffers, including padding (for example 3840x1088 for 3840x1080 video).

method.name: get_decoder
method.description: Returns the decoder, to change its settings before [method open].

method.name: get_media_source
method.description: Returns the [MediaSource] given to [method open_source], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_frame_time
method.description: Returns the time of the frame on screen, or -1.

method.name: get_last_error
method.description: Returns the last error.

method.name: get_plane_rd_rid
method.description: Returns the [RenderingDevice] texture of a plane of the frame on screen. It changes with every frame.

method.name: get_decode_path
method.description: Returns [code]"hardware"[/code] (the V4L2 decoder, frames imported without copies), [code]"software"[/code] (the fallback, see [member software_fallback]), or an empty string when nothing is open.

method.name: get_decode_path_text
method.description: [method get_decode_path] for people: [code]"hardware (VP9)"[/code], [code]"hardware (VP9, 10-bit)"[/code], [code]"hardware (10-bit)"[/code], [code]"hardware"[/code], [code]"software"[/code] or an empty string. Also [code]decode_path_text[/code] in [method get_stats] and [method get_overlay_stats].

method.name: get_software_reason
method.description: On the software path: why the hardware path wasn't used (the same sentence as [code]hw_unsupported_reason[/code] in [method MediaSource.get_video_info]).

method.name: get_next
method.description: Returns the item set with [method set_next], until it takes over (then [code]null[/code]).

method.name: get_overlay_stats
method.description: For a stats overlay, once or twice a second (rates are measured since the previous call). [code]decode_path[/code], [code]position[/code], [code]frame_size[/code], [code]packing[/code]; the stream ([code]codec[/code], [code]video_size[/code], [code]fps[/code], [code]bit_depth[/code]); bitrate: [code]video_kbps[/code] (the last 3 known seconds), [code]video_kbps_history[/code] (the last 60 s, oldest first, -1 unknown; see [method MediaSource.get_video_bitrate_history]), [code]file_kbps[/code]; queue depths from the file to the screen: [code]network_buffered_mb[/code], [code]network_buffered_seconds[/code], [code]network_read_mbps[/code], [code]network_stalls[/code] (smb:// only), [code]demux_video_queue[/code] (packets), [code]demux_video_queue_seconds[/code], [code]demux_video_queue_mb[/code], [code]audio_buffered_seconds[/code], [code]audio_underruns[/code], [code]decoder_input_queue[/code] (access units in the hardware decoder), [code]decoder_capture_free[/code] (picture buffers it can fill), [code]decoder_latency_ms[/code], [code]frames_ready[/code] (decoded, waiting for their time), [code]frames_shown[/code], [code]frames_dropped[/code], [code]decode_errors[/code]; rates (from the second call on): [code]interval_seconds[/code], [code]decode_fps[/code], [code]shown_fps[/code], [code]dropped_per_second[/code], [code]process_cpu_percent[/code] (of one core, all threads); and everything [method get_system_stats] returns.

method.name: get_packing
method.description: Returns how the plane textures hold the samples of the current decoder buffers. The shader must unpack [constant PACKING_TP10_RGBA8] and [constant PACKING_TP10_RGB10A2] itself, with [code]texelFetch[/code] (see [member q10c_view]).

method.name: get_plane_texture
method.description: Returns a texture that always shows the given plane (0: Y, 1: CbCr) of the frame on screen.

method.name: get_position
method.description: Returns the clock in seconds.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns the decoder's [method V4L2Decoder.get_stats] plus [code]frames_shown[/code], [code]frames_dropped[/code] (late), [code]frames_stale[/code] (from before a seek), [code]frames_skipped[/code] (decoded on the way to a seek target), [code]settling[/code], [code]seek_target[/code], [code]position[/code], [code]frame_time[/code] and [code]next_preroll_seconds[/code] (from [method set_next] until the next item's first frame was ready; -1 until then).

method.name: get_system_stats
method.description: The GPU clock, temperatures and battery power from sysfs, whatever the device has (the paths are found on the first call): [code]gpu_mhz[/code], [code]gpu_max_mhz[/code] and [code]gpu_devfreq[/code] (the GPU's devfreq entry), [code]temperature_max_c[/code] and [code]temperature_max_zone[/code] (the hottest thermal zone), [code]cpu_temperature_c[/code] and [code]gpu_temperature_c[/code] (the hottest zone whose type names it), [code]battery_power_w[/code] (power_now, or current_now times voltage_now), [code]battery_percent[/code], [code]battery_status[/code]. Keys the device lacks are left out. The environment variable [code]HWVIDEO_SYSFS_ROOT[/code] reads a fake tree instead (tests).

method.name: get_visible_rect
method.description: Returns the visible rectangle inside the decoded buffer, in pixels.

method.name: get_visible_uv_rect
method.description: Returns the visible rectangle in UV coordinates of the plane textures.

method.name: has_frame
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once a frame is on screen.

method.name: is_finished
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the input has ended, every frame was shown, and the last one has been up for its duration (one frame at the stream's rate). With a [MediaSource] whose audio has finished, [code]true[/code] as soon as the last frame is shown: the audio clock stops at the end of the audio. The boundary is the end of the video, so audio that runs on past it is cut.

method.name: is_playing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the clock runs.

method.name: open
method.description: Opens the decoder (see [method V4L2Decoder.open]). The first frame is shown as soon as it is decoded; the clock starts with [method play].

method.name: open_source
method.description: Plays the video stream of an open [MediaSource], with frame times from the stream's PTS. Play [method MediaSource.get_audio_stream] in an [AudioStreamPlayer] and pass its clock to [method update]. Seeks made on the source (by [method seek], the audio player or directly) are picked up in [method update] from its serial: ready frames are dropped as stale, the clock jumps to the target, and nothing is shown until the frame at the target is known (frames between the keyframe and the target count as [code]frames_skipped[/code]).

method.name: pause
method.description: Stops the clock.

method.name: play
method.description: Starts the clock.

method.name: seek
method.description: With a [MediaSource]: [method MediaSource.seek] (audio and video). With a raw file only 0 works ([method seek_to_start]).

method.name: seek_to_start
method.description: Sets the clock to 0 and decodes from the start again. The current frame stays on screen until the first new one.

method.name: set_next
method.description: The next item, for a change without a gap (groundwork for a playlist). [param next] is opened with [method open_source] and not played. From now on this texture's [method update] also updates [param next], which decodes and holds its first frame (a few frames ahead at most: its decoder's lead time) and then waits. Its [MediaSource] reads ahead its queues and stops. Once this one [method is_finished], [method update] calls [method swap_planes_with], so a material that samples this texture's plane textures goes on with [param next]'s frames, without changing a parameter. It then calls [method HWVideoTexture.play] on [param next] and emits [signal next_started]. From there on, call [method update] on [param next], with the clock of its source's audio stream, and close this one. The swap happens in the [method update] in which this item's last frame has been shown for its duration: the next item's first frame is on screen at the next draw. On the host's software path, the next item was ready 40 ms after this call. While it waited, its threads used 0.3 % of a core and it held about 60 MB more. The hardware path holds a second set of decoder buffers meanwhile. [code]next_preroll_seconds[/code] in [method get_stats] is the time until its first frame was ready. [code]null[/code]: none.

method.name: swap_planes_with
method.description: Exchanges the plane textures ([method get_plane_texture]) with [param other]'s and points each set at its new owner's current frame (the placeholder if it has none yet). A material that samples the textures this one had now shows [param other]'s frames, and the other way round. [signal format_changed] is emitted on both, since the two may differ in size and packing. [method set_next] uses it at the end of an item; call it directly to change items somewhere else.

method.name: switch_to_software
method.description: With a [MediaSource]: closes the decoder, seeks the source to the current position and goes on there in software (up to [member software_max_pixels]), keeping play or pause and the next item ([method set_next]). [method get_software_reason] is then [param reason]. The picture is black until the first software frame is up (tens of milliseconds). [method update] does this by itself when a VP9 hardware session fails (see [member hw_vp9]); on the software path it restarts the software decoder at the position.

method.name: update
method.description: While playing, advances the clock by [param delta], or sets it to [param master_clock] if that is 0 or more (for example the audio position). During [method MediaSource.trick_play] it advances by [param delta] times the trick speed and ignores [param master_clock]. Then shows the newest decoded frame whose time is at or before the clock and drops the older ones.

members.member: VP9 (profiles 0 and 2) in hardware. On the Frame, sequential VP9 sessions work but two at once crash the decoder firmware (SteamOS #2865), so the process keeps at most one hardware VP9 session ([method V4L2Decoder.is_vp9_session_live]): [method open_source] of VP9 while another texture holds it (the next item, picture in picture, thumbnails, a crossfade) decodes in software, with a log line and the reason in [method get_software_reason], or fails if software can't take it. A VP9 hardware session that fails (DQBUF errors, a run of decoder errors, no picture for the input fed, a hang; or 10-bit without P010) stops cleanly and [method update] goes on in software from the current position ([method switch_to_software]); after a decoder fault, hardware VP9 stays off until the process ends ([method V4L2Decoder.get_vp9_disabled_reason]). [code]false[/code]: VP9 always in software. The environment variable [code]HWVIDEO_HW_VP9=0[/code] or [code]1[/code] overrides it. Applies at [method open_source].

0.25 to 4. Without a master clock ([method update] with [code]master_clock[/code] below 0), the frame clock runs this much faster or slower. With the audio as the master clock, set [member MediaSource.playback_speed] instead: the video follows the audio.

When [method open_source] gets a stream the hardware path can't show (10-bit without P010, 4:2:2, H.264 High 10, VP9 under the rules of [member hw_vp9]), or there is no hardware decoder (no [member V4L2Decoder.device_path], as on a desktop), it is decoded in software instead if it is H.264, HEVC or VP9 of at most [member software_max_pixels]: FFmpeg's decoders on threads of their own, each frame converted to 8-bit NV12 and uploaded to two textures, so [method get_plane_texture] and the NV12 shader work the same. 10-bit is rounded to 8 bits and HDR isn't tone-mapped. Bigger or other streams fail with the reason in [method get_last_error]. [method get_stats] then has [code]decode_path[/code] [code]"software"[/code], the keys of [method V4L2Decoder.get_stats] that apply, and [code]software_*[/code] keys ([code]software_thread_cpu_seconds[/code] is the feeding thread only; [code]process_cpu_seconds[/code] includes FFmpeg's worker threads). [method open] (raw Annex-B files) always uses the hardware path. After opening and after a seek, the software decoder skips the pictures nothing refers to (most B-frames) until two frames before the target, since those would be thrown away: seeks settle faster and cost less CPU. The environment variable [code]HWVIDEO_SW_SEEK_NONREF=0[/code] turns that off. The environment variable [code]HWVIDEO_FORCE_SW=1[/code] decodes in software every stream it can, also on the Frame, to compare the two paths; bigger streams still go to the hardware.
The largest frame (width x height) decoded in software: 1920 x 1088 by default.
FFmpeg decoder threads on the software path (frame and slice threading).

Experimental, with [member V4L2Decoder.experimental_10bit]: how a 10-bit decoder buffer ([code]Q10C[/code], UBWC-compressed TP10) is imported. Turnip has no TP10 format, but each plane of a Q10C buffer is laid out like a UBWC image of a 32-bit format, a third of the width in texels, and the Adreno 750 can read UBWC data as another format. Each texel is then a 32-bit word with three 10-bit samples (bits 0-9, 10-19, 20-29); the CbCr plane holds Cb and Cr alternately. [code]"rgb10a2"[/code] imports the planes as A2B10G10R10 (the three samples are r, g and b), [code]"rgba8"[/code] as R8G8B8A8 (the shader rebuilds the word from the bytes). The [code]_mutable[/code] variants make the images mutable to a format of another UBWC class, which on the A750 sets the descriptors' bit for reading UBWC across formats. Which, if any, gives a correct picture is what the experiment is for.

signal.name: format_changed
signal.description: Emitted when a new set of decoder buffers was imported: the decoded size or visible rectangle may have changed. Also emitted on both by [method swap_planes_with].

signal.name: next_started
signal.description: Emitted by [method update] when the item set with [method set_next] has taken over the plane textures and started playing. Play its source's audio stream now, update [param next] from the next frame on, and close this one.

constants.constant: Y as R8 (reads as luminance) and interleaved CbCr as R8G8 at half size (reads as luminance and alpha): NV12 and Q08C buffers.
Q10C: each texel is a 32-bit word of three 10-bit samples, as R8G8B8A8 (the word's bytes, least significant in r).
Q10C: each texel is a 32-bit word of three 10-bit samples, as A2B10G10R10 (the samples are r, g and b).

P010 (10-bit, linear): Y as R16 in [code]r[/code] and interleaved CbCr as R16G16 at half size (Cb in [code]r[/code], Cr in [code]g[/code]), each sample's 10 bits in the high bits of 16. Multiply by [code]65535.0 / 65280.0[/code] to get the 8-bit scale (64-940 becomes 16-235). Used when the decoder offers P010 (see [method V4L2Decoder.is_p010_available]).
